components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--color-card); color: var(--color-foreground); border-radius: 8px; padding: 32px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.25), 0 8px 24px -12px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.5); font-family: 'Figtree Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-card-head { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-family: 'Source Serif 4 Variable', Georgia, serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.33; } .ds-card-n { color: var(--color-muted-foreground); margin-right: 8px; } .ds-claim { margin: 12px 0 0; max-width: 48rem; font-family: 'Source Serif 4 Variable', Georgia, serif; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.375; } .ds-claim a { color: inherit; text-decoration: underline dotted; text-underline-offset: 4px; } .ds-claim a:hover { color: var(--color-primary); } .ds-period { font-family: 'Figtree Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-muted-foreground); } .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; flex-shrink: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-border); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-muted-foreground); } .ds-chip-some { color: var(--color-foreground); }

components.name: Section Chip
components.description: Hairline pill counting how many of a section's checks hold; green when all hold, red when none, muted when nothing is evaluated.
components.html: 1 of 2 hold 2 of 2 hold 0 of 2 hold needs more history
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 10px; font-family: 'Figtree Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-muted-foreground); } .ds-chip-all { color: var(--color-positive); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-positive) 40%, transparent); } .ds-chip-none { color: var(--color-negative); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-negative) 40%, transparent); }

components.css: .ds-snowflake { width: 100%; max-width: 340px; height: auto; font-family: 'Figtree Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-sf-halo { fill: none; stroke: var(--color-muted); stroke-width: 12; opacity: 0.5; } .ds-sf-ring { fill: none; stroke: var(--color-border); stroke-width: 1; } .ds-sf-ring-outer { stroke-width: 1.5; } .ds-sf-blob { fill: var(--color-primary); fill-opacity: 0.78; stroke: var(--color-primary); stroke-width: 2; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-sf-dot { fill: var(--color-primary-foreground); stroke: var(--color-primary); stroke-width: 1.5; } .ds-sf-label { fill: var(--color-foreground); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview:
NTX reads like a printed stock report laid on a dark desk: a gunmetal night ground, one raised gunmetal card per question, fog silver type, and a single molten orange accent that marks the thing the reader is meant to look at (the snowflake, the primary button, the active section, the price line). Serif headings and serif claim sentences carry what the filings say; a humanist sans carries the figures, labels and chrome. Nothing on the page recommends; colour that reads as a verdict (green, red) is spent only where the data itself has a direction.

The world is dark by default (`mode-watcher` sets `defaultMode="dark"`). A light variant exists under `:root` with the same roles; its values live in the sidecar (`.impeccable/design.json`, `colorMeta.*.light`), not here, so the frontmatter stays one source of truth for the shipped default.

Scope note. Only the company page (`/company/[symbol]`), its header card, snowflake, and the sidebar were rebuilt in this world. Home, the company list, hydro and mutual fund routes inherit the tokens in `layout.css` but still carry their older compositions; nothing about their layout, chrome or chart language is recorded here as system. When those routes are rebuilt, extend this file from what ships.
keyCharacteristics: Dark gunmetal ground, cards one step lighter, hairline borders one step lighter again; depth is tonal plus one soft shadow.
One accent, molten orange; green and red are reserved for direction and verdict.
Serif for headings, claim sentences and the headline price; sans for everything else; tabular numerals everywhere.
Sections are numbered report cards: number + title, a verdict chip, one claim sentence, a two-column checks list.
Icons are Lucide line glyphs at 14-16px, used only to mark verdicts and actions.

rules.name: The One Flame Rule
rules.body: Orange is a pointer, not a palette. On any screen it marks at most: the snowflake, one primary button, one active nav item, one price line. If a second orange element is a decoration rather than a pointer, remove it.

rules.name: The Direction Rule
rules.body: Green and red mean one of two things only: a price moved that way, or a published check holds / fails. They never colour headings, backgrounds, chips at rest, or anything a reader could mistake for advice.

rules.name: The Ground-on-Accent Rule
rules.body: Text on orange, green or red is the ground colour (`*-foreground` tokens), not white. The accent glows against the night; it does not carry a white label.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif for headings, claim sentences and the headline price; sans for figures, labels, lists, chrome. A serif figure is only allowed where it is the page's single headline number.

rules.name: The Linked Number Rule
rules.body: A number inside a claim sentence is a link to its evidence: dotted underline, 4px offset, orange on hover. Prose that cannot point at a row does not get a number.

rules.name: The One Column of Cards Rule
rules.body: The company page is a single vertical stack of full-width cards; nothing sits beside a card except the sidebar. Two-column layouts live inside cards, never between them.

rules.name: The Breathing Anchor Rule
rules.body: Every section is an anchor target with 24px scroll margin; the sidebar highlights the topmost visible section using an observer with a `-10% 0 -60% 0` root margin so long sections stay active while read.

rules.name: The Tonal Step Rule
rules.body: Each layer is exactly one lightness step above the one it rests on (ground 0.17 → card 0.215 → popover/active 0.235 → secondary 0.27 → border 0.3). Do not introduce a surface between steps or skip one.

rules.name: The Soft Lift Rule
rules.body: The only shadow is `--shadow-card`. No hard offset shadows, no inner shadows, no glows other than the orange tints listed above.

rules.name: The 8/6 Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are 8px, controls are 6px, counters are round. There is no 12px+ radius in the shipped company page even though `rounded.xl` is defined.

dos: Open every section with its number, its serif title, its chip and the one sentence the filings support, in that order.
Spend orange only as a pointer: snowflake, primary button, active section, price line, flat change.
Colour green or red only for price direction and check verdicts, and set text on them in the ground colour.
Keep every figure in tabular numerals and every claim number as a dotted link to its evidence.
Separate cards by the tonal step and `--shadow-card`; separate items inside cards with hairlines.
Use Lucide line icons at 14-16px for verdicts and actions only.
End any snowflake or rating explanation with "Not a recommendation."
donts: Don't give a card a border, a header strip, or a second shadow.
Don't set a label above a title as an eyebrow or kicker; uppercase labels head lists (HOLDS, WATCH) or ride the snowflake's arcs, nothing else.
Don't introduce a third verdict colour; Watch and Needs-more-history are `muted-foreground`, and `caution` stays reserved until the build uses it.
Don't draw the snowflake as a polygon, add a sixth axis, or weight an axis; the API's verdicts are the rule.
Don't put white text on orange, green or red.
Don't use a radius other than 8px for surfaces, 6px for controls (4px for site nav links), or full for pills.
Don't describe home, company list, hydro or mutual fund layouts as this system; they inherit tokens only until rebuilt.
